_documentation.scope: Every model Eco knows about. `shipping: true` is the user-facing catalog that getCatalog() returns and every user-facing surface reads; `shipping: false` is the dev-only eval lane, reachable through getEvalCandidateModels() and the loopback-gated validation proxy alone (403 in production). One file, two lanes, one flag between them - there is no second catalog.
_documentation.tier_note: `tier` names the device class an entry is the DEFAULT pick for, per slot. selection/recommend.ts walks capable -> laptop -> phone -> floor and takes the first rung the device can actually run, so a graduation is a catalog edit rather than an id literal in the engine. `{}` means the entry is nobody's default and is reachable by fit score alone. Eval-lane entries carry no tier: they are never recommended.
_documentation.license_note: Every entry carries a `license` block describing the license of the model WEIGHTS (separate from Eco's own AGPL-3.0 code license). Eco redistributes those weights, so Apache-2.0 §4(a) and LFM Open License v1.0 §4(a) require recipients to get the license text: `license.textFile` names the verbatim copy under catalog/licenses/ that ships in the bundle, is rendered at /licenses, and is uploaded next to the weights by scripts/mirror-models-to-r2.mjs. `license.artifactLicenseFile` is non-null only where the download repo itself carries a LICENSE at the pinned revision (verified over HTTP); those paths are also in artifact.files so the download itself includes it. `upstreamRepo` is the ORIGINAL author's repo, never the repack we download from. `confirmed: false` means the publisher declares the license but the declaration is self-inconsistent or unverified.
_documentation.generation_note: Every entry's `generation` block is the model's COMPLETE sampling description: a base row plus per-intent overrides, resolved as `{ ...base, ...intentOverrides[intent] }`. An override may restate a base value — recorded as authored so a future retune of the base does not silently move an intent tuned to its own number. Provenance by model: Qwen3 uses the family's published thinking-mode defaults (temp 0.6 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20); Qwen3.5-2B holds top_p at 0.8, the vendor non-thinking ceiling, kept on NO-REGRESSION evidence and NOT as a CJK fix — a real-WebGPU A/B on 2026-06-11 (runs wave25-cjk-fix-r1/r2) showed the reproducible s1 leak (the token for methane) recurs at 0.8, so `suppressCjkTokens` is the actual fix; LFM2/LFM2.5 follow Liquid's published low-temp factual recs; Gemma-4 on LiteRT keeps only the controls LiteRT-LM Web 0.13.1 can honor (sampler type / temperature / top_k / top_p / seed — no repetition penalty, no n-gram ban). NO shipping entry sets `noRepeatNgramSize`: Transformers.js applies that ban across the FULL sequence, prompt included (verified by instantiating NoRepeatNGramLogitsProcessor from the pinned 4.2.0 package at generation step 0 with prompt tokens only), so it forbids handing the user their own words back — the corruption class a chat-experience quality audit recorded. `repetitionPenalty` is the loop guard instead.
_documentation.max_new_tokens_note: `maxNewTokens` is the model's length budget. The cap for an intent is `min(intentTokens[intent] ?? default, max, ceiling)`. `ceiling` is the model's own generation ceiling — the largest number of new tokens it may be asked for under ANY intent — and context-window selection reserves against it before the turn's intent is known.
_documentation.artifact_note: Each model's `artifact` is the canonical download contract. `hfId` + `revision` + `files` feed the server-side proxy allowlist via apps/web/src/lib/local-model-registry.ts (getProxyAllowedLocalModelRegistryArtifacts), and every file MUST have a matching entry in artifact-metadata.json (the proxy's size/SHA-256 verification source — catalog.test.ts pins this invariant). Bootstrap reads this to build the DownloadPlan; mismatches surface as 403 from the proxy. Eval-lane per-file metadata lives in artifact-metadata-eval.json instead, so artifact-metadata.json stays 1:1 with the shipping catalog.

_provenance.tier: DERIVED from a measured ranking defect (FR-2) — the universal `floor` rung for BOTH slots, tried last on every device. On a WebGPU device that can't run the 8GB-floor 1.2B family (sub-8GB memory) yet isn't wasm-only, natural fit-ranking otherwise surfaces LFM2.5-350M — a 0.35GB extraction-type model wrong for chat — as the "Recommended" pick by a ~0.004 margin over the PROVEN qwen3-0.6b. This rung prefers the proven 0.6B chat floor instead. On a `wasm-only` device it sits BELOW the `phone` rung (the requireWasmOnly CPU picks win there) but above nothing else. Where qwen3-0.6b is itself unassignable (e.g. a shader-f16-less adapter, where only the 350M's onnx-q4 loads) this is a safe no-op and natural ranking applies — the 350M stays the honest only option. Falsifier: a fit-scoring change that makes the natural ranking put a chat-appropriate model on top for the sub-8GB WebGPU band, which would make this rung redundant rather than corrective.

compat._rationale: 'unknown' is included: a user-agent we cannot classify gets the same unvalidated-browser tier as safari/firefox rather than a categorical rejection. The capability probes (WebGPU/WASM, memory floor, CPU-EP) plus the first-use smoke gate are the real gate — the UA class was the only thing wholesale-declining these users. Premium models stay engine-validated (chromium-only), so this only opens the conservative floor tier.

compat._rationale: 4GB floor (device-coverage audit, 2026-08-17): the browser's reported device-memory value caps at 8 and rounds DOWN to {..,2,4,8}, so every real 5-7GB laptop reports 4. An 8 floor is therefore a binary 'reports exactly 8' gate that demoted the entire 4-7GB band to the weak qwen3-0.6b / 350m floor — for a model whose download is only 0.76GB. The 4GB floor recovers that band to the good 1.2B; the first-use smoke gate + the >=2-download-fail demotion backstop the rarer genuine-4GB device. (The 8GB floor was inherited from the heavier Bonsai/2B precedent, never measured for this build.)

_provenance.starterFloor: DERIVED (device-coverage audit, finding COV-3 — fixed) — the default instant-start floor: the smallest, f16-free starter rung most devices fall back to. It is EXEMPT from the download-fail auto-demotion because demoting the floor would leave a device with nothing offerable and break instant-start. Repeated download failures of even this model are an environmental dead-end the demotion can't fix, so we never remove it. NOT literally universal: on a `wasm-only` device this build is unassignable (its block-quantized embeddings emit GatherBlockQuantized, unimplemented on the CPU EP — see compat.cpuEpIncompatible), so the `eco-fast` `phone` rung is the effective floor there. The exemption therefore cannot be keyed to this one entry alone; `isDemotionExemptFloor` also exempts the wasm-only floor on a wasm-only device and the `compat.webkitMobileValidated` entry on iOS/WebKit, so a runnable low-end device whose sole assignable model has a couple of transient download failures is never declined below its floor for the 7-day window. Falsifier: a device class where all three exemption clauses miss and a two-download-failure device is still declined below floor.
_provenance.tier.eco-fast: MEASURED 2026-09-01: tier-walk vs scorer diff over 750 profiles, the only assignable model on these cells — f16-less Safari/non-Chromium WebGPU (84 cells). On devices that run WebGPU but lack the `shader-f16` feature — older-Intel desktops (C2) and ~all Adreno Android (C3) — every q4f16 ONNX/MLC build is unassignable, but Gemma 4 (LiteRT, non-f16 `.litertlm`) loads fine. Where Gemma is ALSO unassignable (low-memory / WASM-only / non-Chromium) it never enters the ranked list, so holding this rung is a safe no-op and natural fit-score ranking applies unchanged. NOTE: retiring this lane is a Phase R7 decision requiring a written comparison — it is the ONLY second choice f16-less devices have.
_provenance.maxNewTokens.ceiling: DERIVED — 1024 is the loosest generation-to-context ratio already in use on a shipping model (LFM2.5-1.2B runs 2048 against a 4096 context). The previous 2048 ceiling against this entry's 2048 contextTokens left no room for the system prompt or history: an s33 measurement saw only 2 of 10 messages survive selection. The context half of that falsifier was met on 2026-09-01 (contextTokens is now MEASURED at 32768); the ceiling is deliberately left at 1024 in that change — raising it changes reply length on a shipping default, a Phase M length decision, not a context-window one.
_provenance.capabilities.contextTokens: MEASURED (2026-09-01, s37 context-stress probes on a production build, Apple Silicon, Chrome 152; eco-notes decisions/data/s37-r5b-measurements.md §1) — with the engine's maxNumTokens set to 32768 the model loaded and passed verbatim two-fact recall at ~4.4k / 6.7k / 7.9k / 10.8k / 12.0k prompt tokens (TTFT 5.1 / 7.7 / 9.2 / 13.1 / 14.1 s), 5–7× faster prefill than the transformers lane on the same prompts. 32768 is the publisher's stated window and the largest value probed. The previous 2048 was INHERITED (an earlier note attributed it to the model card's web/CPU/GPU builds; the run contradicts that reading) and, passed as maxNumTokens, made the engine THROW on any prompt past it (`Input token ids are too long … 6721 >= 2048`) rather than truncate. This lane has no tokenizer, so the history window is chosen on a one-character-per-token upper bound: contextTokens = N keeps at most N characters (≈ N/4 real tokens), so at 32768 the worst real prompt is ~8k tokens, inside the passing range, and the engine's own limit is unreachable. Falsifier: a recall failure or engine error below ~8k real tokens on a device we ship this entry to (compat: WebGPU, ≥ 8 GB, Chromium).
_provenance.maxNewTokens.intentTokens: INERT AS WRITTEN — `deep`, `file` and `research` are authored at 1536 but the 1024 `ceiling` clamps all three, so each currently resolves to 1024. The authored numbers are kept, not lowered: they are the intended budgets for when the context question is settled, and they become live again the moment a stress probe justifies raising the ceiling. Read the resolved value as `min(intentTokens[intent] ?? default, max, ceiling)`, not as this table alone.

compat._rationale: Gemma 4 E2B via LiteRT (the f16-less C2/C3 answer — model-offering overhaul 2026-06-29). LiteRT is WebGPU-only and Chromium-only by construction (runtime/litert-adapter.ts), so requireWebgpu + chromium. Crucially its `litertlm` format does NOT need shader-f16 (formatRequiresShaderF16 -> false), so the f16 gate keeps it ASSIGNABLE on f16-less adapters where every q4f16 model is filtered out — exactly the desktop-Intel / Adreno-Android hole it fills. 8GB floor matches Bonsai/Qwen (mmap keeps resident weights ~0.8GB of the ~1.9GB download). warnIfMobile: real Android per-tab memory is unvalidated (Track C C3 is provisional) — offered with a caveat, smoke-gated.

Granite-4.0-350M (onnx-q4) is the most capable CPU-safe model in the catalog (class-leading 350M IFEval) — a genuine quality step up over the 360M SmolLM2 fast floor. Its q4 build clears the CPU EP (loads + generates coherently, no GatherBlockQuantized, so not cpuEpIncompatible) and is assignable on wasm-only devices with >=4GB. models.knownLimitation: Validated on high-memory Chromium WebGPU; a larger, slower download than the lighter Eco Fast model, and other browsers, low-memory devices, and a second machine are not yet proven.

models._laneNote: Phase-2 lane candidate, parked non-viable: the 1.43GB single-file q4f16 ONNX std::bad_allocs at onnxruntime-web session creation even on 16GB. Retry needs an external-data build.
models.bestFor: Instruction-tuned chat and reasoning; the larger Qwen3 sibling for higher quality.
models.knownLimitation: Non-viable in Eco's browser runtime: 1.43GB single-file q4f16 ONNX std::bad_allocs on onnxruntime-web session creation (even on 16GB). Retry needs an external-data build.

models._laneNote: A-3 load-peak decomposition cell (2026-07-16): the SAME Qwen3-0.6B weights the catalog serves, but the repo's fp32-initializer q4 artifact, so the sustained-memory probe can test whether the fp16->fp32 initializer conversion causes the ~3.1GB ORT session-init RSS spike.
models.bestFor: A-3 measurement cell: the shipping Qwen3-0.6B weights in the fp32-initializer q4 build, to profile ORT session-init load peak without fp16 initializers.
models.knownLimitation: Dev-only load-peak measurement cell — not a shipping default. The q4 artifact is ~0.86GB (larger on disk than the q4f16 build) and exists only to test whether removing fp16 initializers at the source kills the ORT session-init RSS spike.

models._laneNote: A-3 baseline cell retained at the 2026-07-17 external-data graduation: the pre-graduation single-file q4f16 build, kept so its ORT session-init load transient can be A/B'd against the shipping external-data artifact on the same machine and pressure.
models.bestFor: A-3 baseline cell: the pre-graduation single-file q4f16 Qwen3-0.6B build, retained to A/B its ORT session-init load transient against the graduated external-data catalog artifact (same weights, paired measurement).
models.knownLimitation: Dev-only measurement baseline — the single-file build the catalog moved off of. It stages the whole model in the wasm heap at session create (the ~2s load spike the external-data graduation removed); kept only for paired A/B against the shipping external-data build.

models._laneNote: Chat #7 M2 bake-off, high-memory quality tier (leads all <10B on Intelligence Index). Decoder external data ships in TWO chunks, so it also exercises the per-file chunk-map path.
models.bestFor: Bake-off candidate: highest-quality option for high-memory devices (leads all <10B models on Intelligence Index).
models.knownLimitation: Unvalidated in Eco's runtime; ~2.8GB download + multi-chunk decoder targets high-memory WebGPU devices only.

models._laneNote: Chat #7 M2 bake-off, eliminated on evidence (deterministic m2 arithmetic error, slowest decode). Base PTQ q4f16 export consumed text-only; the preferred QAT-mobile q2f16 build is ORT-web-blocked (2-bit GatherBlockQuantized unsupported).
models.bestFor: Bake-off candidate: strongest raw quality in the 2B class; future vision/audio path in the same artifact family.
models.knownLimitation: Unvalidated in Eco's runtime. PTQ q4f16 fallback build (QAT-mobile q2f16 is ORT-web-blocked); ~1.6GB embeddings resident in RAM; ORT-web Gemma fp16 overflow lineage and KV-cache reuse compatibility unverified.

models._laneNote: Community QAT-q4 conversion (nico-martin). RESULT 2026-06-15: DOES NOT LOAD -- downloads and verifies, then hangs indefinitely at ORT-web WebGPU session-create, because the q4 build block-quantizes the 1.76GB embedding table into GatherBlockQuantized, unsupported on ORT-web's WebGPU EP. Kept as the test record; do NOT re-run blind or graduate.
models.bestFor: Bake-off candidate: a quantization-aware-trained (QAT) q4 Gemma 4 E2B (community conversion by nico-martin) — tests whether QAT recovers the quality the base PTQ build lost.
models.knownLimitation: Does NOT load in Eco's runtime (verified 2026-06-15): hangs at onnxruntime-web WebGPU session-create because the q4 build block-quantizes its 1.76GB embedding table → GatherBlockQuantized, unsupported on ORT-web's WebGPU EP. WASM/CPU EP also impractical at this size. Lane-only test record.

models._laneNote: Eval-only sibling of the shipping E2B LiteRT entry: tests whether the larger Gemma 4 LiteRT build improves quality through the same validation-selected path, without changing shipping defaults.
models.bestFor: Eval-only LiteRT evidence candidate: tests whether the larger Gemma 4 LiteRT build improves quality over E2B through the same validation-selected product path, without changing Eco shipping defaults.
models.knownLimitation: Dev-only third runtime (@litert-lm/core, early preview, Chromium WebGPU only). Single 2.97GB .litertlm bundle fetched through Eco's validation-only same-origin proxy; sampling maps temperature/top-k/top-p but has no repetition-penalty knob; KV-cache reuse across turns is not wired in the spike.

models._laneNote: Runtime bake-off cell: the same Qwen3-0.6B weights the catalog serves as ONNX, on the WebLLM/MLC runtime, so diagnostics can compare TTFT, decode throughput, context ceiling and output parity across both runtimes. contextTokens is deliberately 16384 -- the adapter passes it to MLC as context_window_size and the depth probes need ~12k.
models.bestFor: Runtime bake-off cell: the same Qwen3-0.6B weights the catalog serves as ONNX, but on the WebLLM/MLC runtime, so diagnostics can compare both runtimes on identical weights.
models.knownLimitation: Dev-only runtime comparison cell. Not a shipping default; exists only to A/B the MLC runtime against the ONNX runtime on the same model in the eval harness.
